findings.description: W1 PHANTOM REQ ID IN A GROOM-OWNED SLOT LABEL (the only phantom in the milestone) — machine extraction over all 7 cards (every slash-list and ..-range expanded, matched against the 749 canonical ids in docs/requirements.md) found exactly one non-existent citation: `REQ-AI-053` in docs/issues/t35.md line 86, inside the Verification-commands section's ac3 SLOT LABEL ('(REQ-PROD-043, REQ-AI-053/100, REQ-TECH-026)'). The intended id is REQ-ARCH-053 (agent layer directory structure), which t35's own Metadata/Source and ac-body cite CORRECTLY; REQ-AI-053 exists nowhere in docs/requirements.md (the REQ-AI series jumps 052 -> 060) nor in docs/requirements/Chapter9_AIWorkflow.md. Split check: 0 phantoms in the Goal/Metadata/AC-body sections of all seven cards, 0 in the survey handoff, and the plan.md phase_6 'phantoms' a naive scan produces are register-notation ranges (REQ-AI-001..052, REQ-AI-130..134, ...) whose endpoints all exist. CLASSIFICATION: orchestrator ruling (2026-10-10) severity=warning, not error — the contract is intact (the AC body cites the right id) and the defect lives in PLACEHOLDER-class slot text that groom is contracted to rewrite byte-exactly; filing it as an error would trigger review_plan FAIL -> survey regeneration of 7 well-formed cards + platform #32-#38 + rulings 1-8 to produce identical cards. Precedent: phase_5 W2/W3/W4/W5 citation-pin warnings. REMEDY (MANDATORY, groom t35): the pinned ac3 command AND slot label MUST cite REQ-ARCH-053 and MUST NOT contain the token REQ-AI-053. VERIFIER GATE (machine-checkable, fail-before on the phantom): grep -c 'REQ-AI-053' over docs/issues/t35.md must be 0 at verify_issue (currently 1), and the generated/extracted pinned section must contain REQ-ARCH-053. If groom ships the phantom it becomes an error at verify (BUILDER_COMMAND_MISMATCH-class blocker).

W2 CRITERIA-ROW NUMBERING CONFLATION + OFF-BY-ONE ON THE COUNT ROWS — t35's Metadata/Goal/ac5 cite 'criteria §24.1 rows 7/9/10/11/12' and '§24.2 rows 31/32', but read against docs/requirements.md the agent-pack rows live in THREE different tables: §24.3 row 7 ('Agent Extension Pack functional', REQ-EXT-001..083) and row 9 ('Permissions documented', REQ-EXT-060) are the ones t34/t35 mean; §24.1 rows 7/9/10/11/12 are 'User can filter by category'/'User can delete expense'/'set budget'/'update budget'/'delete budget' (nothing to do with the pack); §24.2 rows 31/32 do not exist (that table ends at 20) and §24.1 rows 31/32 are 'User A cannot see User B's data' (REQ-PROD-010/REQ-SEC-030) and 'All five charts visible' (REQ-PROJ-004) — yet ac5 pins '31/REQ-PLAN-061/executed/MCP_TEST_ROWS' and '32/REQ-EXT-072/executed/HOOK_TEST_ROWS'. The hook-tests row is actually §24.3 row 8 ('Hook tests pass', REQ-EXT-072, 'pytest test_agent_hooks.py'), which t30 cites correctly. Additionally the measurable-count rows are §24.4 rows 9/10/11/12 (skills=3, subagents=2, MCP tools=4, hooks=2), so t35's 'criteria rows 10/11/12 (skills=3 / subagents=2 / MCP tools=4 / hooks=2)' is off by one and would drop the skills row; and Criterion 12 belongs to the §24.5 table (row 12, REQ-EXT-001..083). t34's own citations are correct (§24.1 row 9 is quoted by its verification text 'Read docs/permissions.md' which is §24.3 row 9 — t34's Metadata says 'criteria row 9' without a table qualifier, same ambiguity, milder). REMEDY (groom t35, then t34): qualify every mapped row as <table>.<row> (24.3-7, 24.3-8, 24.3-9, 24.4-9, 24.4-10, 24.4-11, 24.4-12, 24.5-12) in the ac5 pins and in the generated document's mapping table, keep the REQ id of each row equal to the REQ id the requirements table itself names for that row, and pin the CRITERIA_NUMBERS header to the table-qualified set. Verifier: cross-check each pinned row id against docs/requirements.md rather than against the card.

W3 COMPOSITE ASSERTS A FLOOR ITS OWN DEPENDENCIES CANNOT REACH — t31's ac6 pins 'backend >= 258 nodes green (the t30 floor)' but t31 depends on t29 ONLY (frontmatter depends: [t29]; dag edges t31->t29 only; verified bidirectionally). t30 (the +14 hook nodes) is a SIBLING, not an ancestor, so a worktree branched at t29 has 244 collected and t31's ac6 is RED for a reason unrelated to t31's own diff — a false-failure gate that depends on merge ORDER, not on the DAG. The survey's batch list ([t29,t30,t31], [t32,t33,t34], [t35]) does imply t30-before-t31, but the DAG does not encode it and nothing in the card says the composite is order-dependent. (The same class exists for t33 — filed separately as W4.) REMEDY (groom t31, pick one and record it): (a) pin t31's ac6 backend leg at >= 244 with the exact-258 assertion deferred to the cards that depend on t30 (cleanest: each card asserts a floor reachable from its declared ancestors; the milestone-exit >= 270 stays in t35), or (b) keep >= 258 and add the ordering to the contract by pinning t31's merge order after t30 in the orchestrator merge plan (NOT a new DAG edge — an added t31->t30 edge would lengthen the milestone-local chain and is not warranted by any artifact dependency). Do not leave the composite order-dependent and undocumented.

W4 COMPOSITE ASSERTS THE t32 FLOOR WITHOUT A t32 DEPENDENCY — t33's ac6 and Definition of Done pin 'backend >= 270 nodes green (the t32 floor; this card adds NO test node)', but t33 depends on t29 ONLY (frontmatter depends: [t29]; dag edge t33->t29 only). t32 is a sibling in batch 2, so at t33's own branch point the collection is 258 (post-t30) and the >= 270 leg is unreachable regardless of t33's diff — the same order-dependent false-red class as W3, one step further along (t33 needs BOTH t30 and t32 merged). t34 and t35 are clean here: both list t32 in depends, so >= 270 is genuinely inherited. REMEDY (groom t33): pin t33's ac6 backend leg at >= 258 (the floor its ancestors can produce) or gate it as '>= 244 + whatever the merged base reports' with the parsed value recorded, and leave >= 270 to t34/t35; alternatively record the merge-order requirement (t33 after t32) in the orchestrator merge plan. Either way the card's own text must stop describing 270 as available to it.

W5 SLOT LABEL PINS A WRONG MAX_AMOUNT — t30's ac1 SLOT label reads 'defines MAX_AMOUNT = 1000000' while the AC BODY (authoritative) pins `MAX_AMOUNT = Decimal("999999999.99")`, and the merged backend ceiling is `AMOUNT_MAX = Decimal("999999999.99")` — re-measured today at backend/app/schemas/expense.py:41 and backend/app/services/expense_service.py:46. If groom pins from the slot, ac4's equality gate against the imported backend constant fails and the hook is 800x too strict (a real product defect, not a typo in a comment). REMEDY (groom t30): pin from the AC BODY value Decimal("999999999.99"); name the imported symbol exactly (the merged constant is AMOUNT_MAX, the hook's is MAX_AMOUNT — pin `from app.schemas.expense import AMOUNT_MAX` and the equality assertion hook.MAX_AMOUNT == AMOUNT_MAX); and correct the slot label so the two never disagree again.

W6 DEFINITION-OF-DONE FLOOR DIVERGES FROM THE PINNED mypy POLICY — t30's Definition of Done says 'mypy >= 84 files' while its own ac6 pins 'mypy >= 83 source files (the FLOOR IS UNCHANGED; the observed count grows by one with the new test file — groom records the observed value, it does not raise the floor)', which is exactly plan.md phase_6 ruling 5 ('mypy stays >= 83 for the whole milestone ... t24..t28 all pinned >= 83 and none refreshed it'). Re-measured today: `uv run mypy .` -> 'Success: no issues found in 84 source files' (84 is the PRE-milestone observed value, so a >= 84 floor is accidentally green now but silently becomes a refreshed floor, contradicting the ruling and the other six cards). REMEDY (groom t30): rewrite the DoD line to '>= 83 (observed: <N> at merge, recorded not pinned)' so the whole milestone keeps one floor and one recorded observation, per ruling 5.

W7 SLOT LABELS DRIFT FROM AC-BODY SEMANTICS IN THREE PLACES (t30) — (a) ac2's slot pins the signature as `validate_ownership(resource_user_id, token_user_id)` while the AC BODY pins `validate_ownership(owner_id: object, user_id: object) -> None`; parameter names are contract at pin time (the 14 frozen node IDs and the test's call sites use them). (b) ac2's and ac3's slots cite REQ-EXT-032/033 and REQ-EXT-038 — those are the MCP configuration/authentication/tool-schema ids of Chapter 10 §10.4 (verified in docs/requirements.md), not hook ids; the hook ids are REQ-EXT-020..025, and ac3's body correctly names the five REQ-EXT-024 headings (trigger, checks, failure behavior, agent behavior, design notes) whereas its slot lists a different set ('purpose, signature, trigger point, failure behavior and the bypass warning'). (c) ac5's slot is an ENTIRELY DIFFERENT GATE from its body: the body is the hermetic attestation that the merged schema/service already enforce the ceiling and ownership (greps on backend/app/schemas/expense.py, services/expense_service.py, auth/dependencies.py), while the slot pins 'backend collection total is parsed and pinned EXACTLY 258 ... and the hook files are not named test_*.py'. REMEDY (groom t30): pin every command from the AC BODY, not the slot label; where they disagree the body is authoritative; move the collection-count/purity assertion into ac5's body text or into ac6 (it is already covered by ac6's exact-258 leg) so no AC is verified by a command that does not test it; fix the three mis-attributed REQ ids.

W8 __init__.py OWNERSHIP CONTRADICTED INSIDE t31 — the AC BODY of ac1 says `mcp-server/` contains exactly 'config.py, auth.py, server.py, pyproject.toml (tools/, __init__.py, tests and README land in t32)' and the Out-of-scope line repeats that `mcp-server/__init__.py` is t32's; but ac1's SLOT label requires 'config.py, auth.py, server.py, pyproject.toml, __init__.py' at THIS card, and t31's Constraints claim '4 files = max_files budget' while the survey's own granularity note counts t31 at 5 files ('config + auth + server + manifest + __init__'). t32's ac5 also owns both __init__.py files, so pinning them in t31 would make t32's ac5 a restatement and t31's file count 5. REMEDY (groom t31): pin the AC-BODY layout (4 files, no __init__.py), correct the slot label, and keep the granularity note at 4; if the mcp-server package importability genuinely needs __init__.py before t32, move it into t31's body text explicitly (and update the file count + t32 ac5 in the same pass), do not let the slot smuggle it in.

W9 SYSTEMATIC SLOT-LABEL DRIFT ACROSS t29 ac2..ac5 (section sets + off-by-one REQ ids) — the AC BODIES pin the requirement-faithful section sets (ac2 monthly-report: When to Use, numbered steps, report template, warnings, notes per REQ-EXT-011/REQ-AI-061; ac3 add-expense: When to Use, steps, constraints, example per REQ-EXT-012/REQ-AI-062 + 'name the hook validate_amount as the pre-call guardrail'; ac4 budget-check: When to Use, steps, output template per REQ-EXT-013/REQ-AI-063), but the four SLOT labels list a different pinned section set ('When to Use, Inputs, Steps, Output format, Examples, Guardrails') that appears in NO requirement text, add rules the bodies do not require ('month-argument + no-raw-IDs', 'category-must-exist', 'never instructs a direct DB write', 'percentage/remaining interpretation', 'read-only statement'), and cite shifted ids: ac2 slot says REQ-AI-060 (body: 061), ac3 slot REQ-AI-061 (body: 062), ac4 slot REQ-AI-062 (body: 063), ac5 slot REQ-AI-063/064 (body: 064). The ids themselves all EXIST (this is mis-attribution, not a phantom), but REQ-AI-061 is the monthly-report skill, 062 add-expense, 063 budget-check, so a Verifier tracing slot->requirement would gate the wrong skill's text. REMEDY (groom t29): derive each pinned command from the AC body and the requirement text (the five REQ-EXT-011/012/013 section sets are what the chapter names — verified in docs/requirements.md), attach each skill's own REQ-AI-06x id to its own AC, and either drop the extra rules or add them to the bodies first so body and gate stay one contract.

W10 EXACT-270 vs >= 270 FLOOR SEMANTICS UNPINNED (t32/t35) — t32's ac6 says 'backend `270 tests collected` EXACTLY at this card's merge moment ... FLOOR REFRESH IN-TEXT ... every later card uses >= 270', while t35's ac2 body gates 'BACKEND_COLLECTION <N> PASS with N parsed ... and gated >= 270' but its SLOT label pins 'BACKEND_COLLECTION <N>=270' and t35's ac6 says 'backend `270 tests collected` + >= 270 nodes'. An exact-equality collection gate is a maintenance trap: phase_7/phase_8 will add backend tests, and any merged index entry or composite that requires EXACTLY 270 goes red for unrelated later work (this is the same class of defect as the phase_5 broad-guard lesson, just expressed as an exact count). REMEDY (groom t32 then t35): pin exact-equality ONLY at the card that creates the delta (t30: exactly 258; t32: exactly 270) and pin >= 270 everywhere else (t33/t34/t35 composites and t35's BACKEND_COLLECTION row), record the parsed value in the generated document either way, and fix t35's ac2 slot to '>= 270'. Verifier: reject any pinned command that asserts an exact collection count in a card other than t30/t32.

W11 ac3 ALLOWLIST MECHANISM IS THE ONLY SELF-REFERENTIAL GATE IN THE MILESTONE AND IS UNPINNED — t34 ac3 requires the pack doc's verification checklist to carry 'one runnable command line per component ... every command line in that checklist is grep-present in a groom-pinned allowlist of the milestone's real gates'. The allowlist itself is not named anywhere yet, so as written the gate is vacuous (an empty or hand-typed allowlist passes trivially, and a reviewer following a checklist command that does not exist on this host is exactly the failure REQ-EXT-071 exists to prevent). It is also the one AC whose evidence is other cards' commands, which are themselves still PLACEHOLDER_AT_GROOM (t29..t33 are groomed AFTER this milestone's review, in batch order t29,t30,t31 then t32,t33,t34). REMEDY (groom t34, sequenced AFTER t29..t33 grooming): pin the allowlist as an explicit enumerated set of the six already-pinned command strings (skills frontmatter parse, hook pytest, MCP pytest, subagent frontmatter parse, git ls-files/cat-through symlink gate, docs count cross-check), store it in the t34 handoff so the Verifier can diff it, and gate the checklist lines against it with a byte-equality grep (not a substring match). If t34 is groomed before t32/t33, groom MUST re-open it after those pins land rather than inventing placeholder commands.

W12 FORBIDDEN-IMPORT GREP MUST BE ANCHORED, AND THE SUBPROCESS-FREE vs RE-RUN TENSION NEEDS ONE PINNED MECHANISM — t35 ac1 forbids the tokens `subprocess`, `requests`, `uvicorn`, `socket`, `sqlalchemy` in backend/scripts/agent_pack_verification.py. Two hazards measured today: (a) the sibling precedent script backend/scripts/infra_verification.py (t28) carries the literal words in its DOCSTRING ('NO subprocess, NO requests, NO uvicorn') and imports sqlalchemy, so an unanchored `grep -q subprocess` over the new script is either trivially red or vacuously green depending on form — the pin must be `^(import|from) (subprocess|requests|uvicorn|socket|sqlalchemy)` (verified necessary against that file), and the generated document's own DEFERRED/ATTEST text must not contain a forbidden token that a re-run grep would then fail. (b) ac2 requires 'HOOK_TEST_ROWS 14 PASS and MCP_TEST_ROWS 12 PASS (both phase_6 test files re-run hermetically)' but a pytest re-run from a python script needs subprocess (or pytest.main / os.system, which is the same thing in a trench coat); the card's own groom constraints already flag this and demand ONE pinned mechanism. REMEDY (groom t35): pin the mechanism explicitly — recommended: the SCRIPT emits the structural/count rows only, and the two EXECUTED pytest legs are run by the ac2 verification COMMAND (`uv run pytest tests/integration/test_agent_hooks.py -q` and `.../test_mcp_tools.py -q`, counts parsed via `--collect-only -q | grep -c "::"`) whose results are compared against the document's tokens, keeping the script subprocess-free; anchor every forbidden-token grep to import statements; and record the choice in the generated document so the byte-stability leg of ac1 stays deterministic.

W13 STANDING WARN CARRIED FORWARD (not a phase_6 defect) — two structural conditions that every phase_5+ review has passed under and that the orchestrator should keep recording rather than 'fixing': (1) DEP CHAIN: the cumulative critical path is now 24 EDGES against limits.dep_chain_warn = 10 and limits.dep_chain_halt = 20 (docs/config.yaml, operator-owned). Under plan.md phase_6 ruling 8 (orchestrator ruling, 2026-10-10) the thresholds are judged on the MILESTONE-LOCAL reading — phase_6's local maximum is 5 edges (t28->t29->t31->t32->t34->t35), 5 < 20 => PASS — and the cumulative 24 is carried as a WARN-class standing condition, exactly as warn=10 has been carried since phase_2. Not an error, and per the ruling must NOT be closed by flattening the card graph (that would break the t15/t23/t28 verification-card precedent and still breach). (2) DAG-vs-FRONTMATTER ARTIFACT: docs/issues/closed/t19.md is a context-stripped closure summary with no frontmatter, so its t19->t14 edge is dag-only; all 24 other nodes (including all 7 phase_6 cards) match their DAG edges bidirectionally. Identical condition to the one phase_4 and phase_5 were passed under.

warnings.remedy: MANDATORY (groom t35): the pinned ac3 command AND the ac3 slot label MUST cite REQ-ARCH-053 and MUST NOT contain the token REQ-AI-053 (the phantom is at docs/issues/t35.md:86, the Verification-commands section's ac3 label).
